newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary milling wheat futures rise, maize eases.
newsitem.headline: Hungary milling wheat futures rise, maize eases.

text.p: End-of-year profit-taking and speculative trade dominated the grain section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange in heavy turnover, traders said on Tuesday.
"Most speculative traders are deciding to cash in (during the last three days of trade) this year and take advantage of lower taxes," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle brokerage.
Taxation at source will go up to 20 percent as of January 1 from the current 10 percent.
Those who do not want to deliver the January contracts are trying to get out, another trader said, adding that this mainly applied to wheat contracts.
"They try to raise prices by the (400 forint) limit, but no one is willing to sell," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.

Milling wheat prices rose by 170 forints to 400 forints for most maturities, except the January delivery, in which there were no deals, and the September 1997 delivery, which closed at 21,020 forints, down 90.
Other maturities closed between 27,600 forints for March and 23,750 for December.
Maize prices ended mostly 190 to 300 forints lower, except for the untraded January maturity and March 1997 which closed at 19,100 forints, up 200.
"The maize scene was disoriented by rumours that some brokerages would be willing to buy larger quantities at high prices," Herczeg said.
Maize contracts for May and July 1997 delivery were the most traded, with 804 and 884 lots changing hands. The two months closed at 19,400 and 20,000 forints respectively.
Total turnover of the BCE grain section was a substantial 1.38 billion forints, or 3,201 lots, of which 2,203 lots were maize and 888 milling wheat.
(Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts. $1=163.55 forints)
